blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the intermediate level, accrual accounting means quietly adjusting the books at month-end to reflect reality. Sales that have been made but not yet paid become accounts receivable. Expenses that have been incurred but not yet invoiced become accrued expenses. Revenue that has been received in advance becomes deferred revenue.

Each of these adjustments is small, but together they transform a month's raw cash activity into a number that shows how the business actually performed. Whereas cash shows only what the bank did, accrual shows what the business did — which is usually a very different story.

The discipline is to make these adjustments every month, carefully and consistently, so that the P&L means what it says and the balance sheet reflects what really happened.

items.q: According to the text, what do sales that have been made but not yet paid become?
items.why: "Sales that have been made but not yet paid become accounts receivable."

items.q: What is the difference between cash and accrual, according to the text?
options: Cash shows what the bank did; accrual shows what the business did
Cash is more accurate than accrual
Accrual only counts money already received
They always produce the same number
items.why: "Whereas cash shows only what the bank did, accrual shows what the business did."

items.q: What becomes deferred revenue?
options: Sales made but not yet paid
Expenses incurred but not yet invoiced
items.why: "Revenue that has been received in advance becomes deferred revenue."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The P&L should mean what it says.
A monthly cash figure is enough to judge how the business performed.
Small adjustments, taken together, change the picture significantly.
Consistency matters when closing the books.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que o caixa sozinho conta uma história diferente — não basta para avaliar a performance.

items.q: The phrase "which is usually a very different story" suggests that…
options: the bank statement is usually wrong
cash and accrual numbers rarely match
items.why: Inferência: se a história costuma ser diferente, os números de caixa e competência normalmente divergem.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie conduzindo o fechamento mensal com um novo contador. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let's walk through this close together, line by line. The bank statement is only our starting point — it tells us what moved through the account, nothing more. Our job is to turn that raw activity into a P&L that actually means something.

Start with the sales. We shipped a large order to the mill in the last week of the month, but the customer hasn't paid yet. On a pure cash basis, that sale is invisible. So we book it as accounts receivable — the revenue belongs to this month, whether or not the cash has landed.

Now do the same in reverse for costs. The freight company hasn't sent us an invoice yet, but we used the service in June, so we accrue the expense. And that big prepayment a client made for July? That's not our revenue this month — park it as deferred revenue until we deliver.

None of these adjustments is dramatic on its own. But do them every single month, consistently, and the numbers start telling the truth. Skip them, and you're just reading the bank's story, not the company's.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie say the bank statement is?
options: Only the starting point of the close
The final version of the P&L
items.why: "The bank statement is only our starting point."

items.q: How does Sophie handle the large order shipped but not yet paid?
options: She accrues it as an expense
She treats it as deferred revenue
She books it as accounts receivable
She ignores it until the cash lands
items.why: "we book it as accounts receivable — the revenue belongs to this month."

items.q: Why does Sophie treat the client's July prepayment as deferred revenue?
options: Because the company has not delivered yet
Because the freight invoice is missing
Because the service was already used
Because it was paid in cash
items.why: "park it as deferred revenue until we deliver" — a receita só é reconhecida na entrega.

items.q: What does Sophie imply about someone who skips these adjustments?
options: They save valuable time each month
They produce a more accurate balance sheet
They end up reading the bank's story, not the company's
items.why: Inferência: "Skip them, and you're just reading the bank's story, not the company's."

items.q: Why does Sophie stress doing the adjustments "every single month, consistently"?
options: Because consistency is what makes the numbers tell the truth
Because a single adjustment is dramatic on its own
items.why: Inferência: cada ajuste é pequeno, mas a consistência mensal é o que torna os números confiáveis.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We used the courier in June, so we record it as an accrued expense." An accrued expense is a cost that has been…
items.why: Accrued expense = despesa acumulada: já incorrida, mas ainda não faturada.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The client paid us in March for work we deliver in April, so we recorded it as ___."
items.why: Deferred revenue = receita diferida: recebida antes da entrega.

items.q: "These small entries transform the raw cash numbers into a real P&L." To transform means to…
items.why: To transform = transformar, mudar por completo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The whole point of the close is discipline: doing the same ___ every month, consistently."
items.why: Adjustment = ajuste; a lição fala em repetir os ajustes todo mês.

items.q: "A good P&L should reflect what the business actually did." To reflect here means to…
items.why: To reflect = refletir, mostrar fielmente o que aconteceu.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em um fechamento mensal. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The controller still has to sign off on the month-end numbers." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Let's walk through each adjustment together." To walk through means to…
items.why: Walk through = percorrer passo a passo, revisar em detalhe.

items.q: "We need to book the unpaid sale as a receivable." To book an entry means to…
items.why: To book = lançar, registrar na contabilidade.

items.q: "We'll park that prepayment as deferred revenue until we deliver." To park something means to…
items.why: To park = deixar de lado temporariamente, aguardando o momento certo.

items.q: "Do these small entries every month and they really add up." To add up means to…
items.why: Add up = somar-se, tornar-se relevante quando reunidos.
